limits: Single association, not a paired experiment or proof of Air sleep/wake repair.
Scan requests and API call intervals do not measure RF dwell; zero observed records do not prove absence.
PS events are host notifications. Emitted kernel continuity does not restore rate-limited events or prove final wake latency.
Global P/F sequence gaps exclude other peers before target filtering; unobserved boundary events remain unknown.
BATRACE is observed frame/preparation logging and BAMCU is command return; neither proves delivery or operational BA. No aggregate-status inference is made.
Server TCP and client intervals have separate relative starts and rounding; retransmits are not a wire-loss counter.
Final NR/AP restoration is a separate procedure and is not certified by this analysis. The unchanged-router assertion covers the traffic interval only.
Separate associations and observer overhead; this is not a randomized or identical-RF comparison.
ACK establishes receipt at the MAC layer, not client use/adoption. A surviving dip does not prove all NR options ineffective.
Native scan API/request intervals are not measured RF dwell. P/F gaps prevent complete PS-duration or wake-latency inference.
TXFREE status2 is a reported RED-drop HEADER count, not a TCP packet count; queue snapshots are non-atomic.
The configured TCP rate allows catch-up above 600Mbps; matching means do not exclude short troughs.
This follow-up does not establish a new driver fix, full NPU correctness, or repair of the earlier Air stall.

configured_load.authority: Actual iperf start.test_start and command; configured TCP rate is not an instantaneous cap.
